purposeCandidates: candidate: work-surface decision for beginner AI-assisted coding
sharedBrief:
You are advising the HAVEN/CellProtocol project on the design of its developer environment and its first pilot. Answer in English. Do not flatter the design; disagree wherever the reasoning warrants it. State uncertainty explicitly. Ground every verdict in the claim IDs and goal IDs below.

CONTEXT — THE SYSTEM
HAVEN/CellProtocol is a local-first, permissioned data protocol. Functionality is built from 'cells' (owned, permissioned actors with UI 'skeletons' rendered by a web scaffold and a native macOS app called Binding). A staging server runs CellScaffold (Vapor/Swift). A local agent daemon, HAVENAgentD, runs on the user's Mac with its own cells and can bridge staging surfaces to local resources (files, builds, processes). Chat Workbench is the canonical central interface: surfaces are opened from chat. UI must be expressed in the current CellConfiguration/skeleton format; new renderer capabilities are separate decisions. A hard product principle is NO BLOATING: the native app must stay small.

AUDITED EXISTING ASSETS (verified in-repo 2026-07-20; treat as real)
- Chat: ChatCell + scoped AI provider routing; AIGatewayCell (remote providers), LocalLLMGatewayCell (local models).
- Key custody: SecretCredentialCell contract (Book 25) implemented in HAVENAgentD — provider API keys live locally with the agent, never in configs/prompts.
- Model provider catalog + selection contracts (Book 24); NanoGPT (an OpenAI-compatible multi-model aggregator) already used for the project's own multi-model advisory panels.
- Onboarding: GuidedOnboardingCell (personal-copilot flavored); Developer Identity Pack (simulated entities/identities for safe dev, Book 31); signed+notarized pkg with provisioning pack for HAVENAgentD distribution (already piloted).
- Work: TodoCell, WorkItemCell + ProjectPortfolioCell + GitHubWorkSyncCell (GitHub issues import/outbound sync; GitHub stays the primary source), IdeaTaskWorkspaceCell (idea→task→share).
- Social: ParticipationHubCell (invitations, workspace launch), EntityPresenceRegistryCell, public profile cells, purpose-based matching.
- Web embedding: legacy TestCellWebEmbed emits XHTML fragments, but the current portable SkeletonElement enum has no generic WebEmbed/webembed case. An in-app web preview is new renderer/host work and requires a separate security decision.
- Local AI coding CLIs on the pilot machine family: Codex CLI (supports ChatGPT-subscription sign-in) and Claude Code. HAVENAgentD has an allowlisted local-task runtime, a Codex prompt queue, and an MCP handoff, but the current CodexPromptQueue does not launch Codex; a specialized executor/app-server adapter is missing.
- A 2026-07-20 report defines a DeveloperWorkbench plan (docs browser, GitHub work sync, contribution proofs, recognition, quests) in six phases.

THE PILOT
First pilot user is a teenage beginner in Norway, motivated by making things he cares about — plausibly games. Guardian participation is required where provider terms or local rules require it. He wants to learn to use AI tools for coding. Requirements from the task owner:
(a) He must be able to prompt what he wants to build and get to a running result.
(b) He may optionally use his own OpenAI subscription; and he must also be offered a guided setup of a multi-model advisory panel with his own API keys (e.g., NanoGPT), entered during onboarding.
(c) HAVENAgentD should be the local agent doing the work.
(d) The task owner prefers the HAVEN app (Binding) as the primary work surface, with UX on par with Claude Desktop and ChatGPT Desktop (Codex) for this learning loop.
(e) The Developer Workbench must be served from staging but draw on local resources (build, run, files) via the agent.
(f) Evaluate game-development support: it would be attractive to run one or more game engines 'in' the HAVEN app, but the app must not bloat.

GOALS (haven.goal-definition.v1 summaries)
- G1 onboarding-time: minutes from first app open to a first self-prompted project running locally, driven by the pilot user himself. Baseline: not possible today. Target: ≤60 min. Evidence: observed onboarding session log.
- G2 surface-preference: after 2 weeks of use, share of AI-coding sessions the pilot voluntarily runs in the HAVEN app vs Claude Desktop / ChatGPT Desktop. Target: ≥50%. Evidence: session logs/self-report. Sub-checklist for chat-loop parity: streaming responses, code blocks with copy, file/project context, run/build button, error round-trip.
- G3 provider-choice: both provider paths work end-to-end from onboarding UI on staging+local: (path A) OpenAI-subscription route; (path B) own-API-key advisory panel route via NanoGPT with keys held by SecretCredentialCell locally. Evidence: functional verification artifacts.
- G4 gamedev-decision: documented go/no-go on game-engine support with an explicit app-size budget. Evidence: decision log + measured app size delta.

CLAIM LEDGER (haven.claim-definition.v0 summaries; adjudicate each)
- C1 (normative, assertive, owner): The HAVEN app should be the pilot's primary work surface, and UX parity with Claude Desktop/ChatGPT Desktop is achievable for this learning loop. Support: dogfooding value; Chat Workbench + provider routing exist. Standing undercut: parity with dedicated, fast-moving AI-coding UIs is a large surface to match; risk that a frustrating tool teaches the wrong lesson. Scheme: practical reasoning — unexamined critical questions: are alternatives (start him in Codex/Claude Code, migrate later) genuinely worse? What side effects does forcing the surface have on motivation?
- C2 (project_capability, moderated): Existing machinery (SecretCredentialCell in HAVENAgentD + AIGatewayCell + provider catalog) suffices for safe guided onboarding of provider API keys by a beginner. Open premise: a beginner-grade onboarding UX for key entry does not exist yet.
- C3 (factual/project_capability, moderated): The pilot can legitimately use his consumer OpenAI subscription in this environment. Known constraint: a ChatGPT consumer subscription is not an API key; the sanctioned route is Codex CLI/desktop with ChatGPT sign-in. Candidate integration: HAVENAgentD drives local Codex CLI as executor while HAVEN provides the surface. Adjudicate feasibility, ToS-compliance, and maintenance cost.
- C4 (normative, moderated): The core loop should be free-form 'prompt what you want to make' → scaffolded project → agent builds/runs it. Standing rebuttal: beginners may need templates, worked examples, and guardrails more than a blank prompt; a blank prompt can produce unbuildable scope.
- C5 (project_capability, moderated): A staging-served Developer Workbench can draw on local resources via HAVENAgentD cleanly (the CellProtocol cell/bridge architecture makes the wiring natural). Evidence: agent bridge cells exist; provisioning pack solved. Open: security posture of staging↔local execution for a non-expert user's machine.
- C6 (normative/predictive, speculative): HAVEN should support game development without bloating the app. Options on the table: (i) run a web-based runtime (e.g., a JS/WASM engine) in an external local preview first, and only later in a new security-reviewed preview/host surface; there is no current portable generic webembed element; (ii) treat native engines (e.g., Godot) as LOCAL resources installed and orchestrated by HAVENAgentD, with HAVEN as project/asset/learning surface; (iii) actually link an engine into the Binding app (suspected bloat violation). Adjudicate which options respect NO BLOATING while being attractive to a teenage builder.

WHAT TO RETURN (structure your answer exactly like this)
1. Per-claim verdicts C1–C6: supported / contradicted / open, with your reasoning and the single strongest counterargument you can mount.
2. Answers to the unexamined critical questions you consider load-bearing (name which claim they belong to).
3. A concrete recommended architecture/flow for the pilot onboarding (first 60 minutes) and for the daily loop, honoring goals G1–G4.
4. Top 5 risks, each with a mitigation, ranked.
5. The minimal slice you would build first, and what you would explicitly NOT build for this pilot.
Be specific to your assigned role. Firm recommendations, not surveys.

panelists.name: GPT-5.5
panelists.roleInstructions: You own G1 and G2. Design the beginner onboarding (identity, agent install, provider choice incl. key entry via SecretCredentialCell, first prompt-to-running-project) as a concrete step sequence with time budget per step. Judge honestly what 'UX parity with Claude Desktop / ChatGPT Desktop' requires for THIS loop (C1), which parity checklist items are load-bearing for a beginner, and which can be skipped. Be precise about where the skeleton-format UI will strain and what to do within current renderer limits.

panelists.name: Claude-Opus-4.8
panelists.roleInstructions: Steelman both sides of C1 and C4, then adjudicate. Focus on how a teenage beginner actually learns AI-assisted coding: motivation loops, frustration cliffs, scaffolding vs blank prompts, and what makes him come back on day 3 and day 30. Verify the counterarguments in the ledger attack the real arguments, not strawmen. Recommend the learning loop design (templates? quests? free prompting?) and how the social layer (visible progress, showing work to family/friends) should be used without manipulative gamification.

panelists.name: Gemini-3.1-Pro
panelists.roleInstructions: You own C2, C3, C5. Specify the exact integration architecture: staging-served Developer Workbench surfaces + HAVENAgentD local execution; where each provider path terminates (path A: agent drives local Codex CLI with ChatGPT sign-in; path B: AIGatewayCell → NanoGPT with SecretCredentialCell custody); how build/run results flow back to the surface; and the security posture for a non-expert minor's machine (key custody, scope of what staging can ask the agent to do, consent surfaces). Flag any place where the 'easy with CellProtocol' assumption in C5 is doing unearned work.

panelists.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
panelists.roleInstructions: Attack the plan. Priority targets: the UX-parity assumption in C1 (what does chasing two fast-moving desktop apps cost, and what happens when the pilot silently switches tools); ToS/compliance and breakage risk in C3; staging→local execution as an attack path in C5 (a server-served surface asking a local agent to run builds on a family machine); n=1 overfitting (building product for one teenager); privacy of a minor in logs/telemetry; and bloat creep in C6. For each attack, state the concrete failure scenario and the cheapest mitigation. If you think the pilot framing itself is wrong, say so and propose the alternative.

panelists.name: Kimi-K2.6
panelists.roleInstructions: You own C6 and its interaction with G1/G2. Compare the three options (web/WASM runtime in webembed; native engines as agent-orchestrated local resources; linking an engine into the app) on: attractiveness to a teenage builder, time-to-first-playable-thing, AI-assistability (how well can an AI agent write code for this stack), app-size impact, and maintenance. Name concrete engines/runtimes and a recommended default stack for the pilot's first game. Respect NO BLOATING as a hard constraint and give a measurable size budget.

panelists.name: GLM-5.2
panelists.roleInstructions: Evaluate from outside the project's assumptions. Is a single teenage pilot the right first target for the developer environment, or a distraction dressed as validation? What is the minimal slice that serves BOTH the pilot and the general developer-environment plan from the 2026-07-20 report, and what in the current framing should be cut or deferred? Challenge any goal that is not genuinely testable, and propose sharper replacements. Keep the team honest about the difference between 'my kid liked it' and validated learning.
